params.message: steps up to the ATM terminal and makes a deposit.

chitchat: Hock turns something small over under the loupe and names a number lower than it deserves.
"Everything in here belonged to someone who swore they'd be back. They swore."
description: A soft-spoken man behind the wire mesh, loupe screwed into one eye and a valuation already forming behind the other. He buys what walks in, holds what won't sell, and remembers nothing that could be asked about later. Every kindness he offers is priced, and the price is always his.

buy.text: "Anything that'll sit in a case and hold its value till the next desperate soul." He gestures at the wall of tickets. "Tools, trinkets, the odd thing best not described on a receipt. I pay what it's worth to me, which is less than it's worth to you, and that gap is the whole business. Bring it round, I'll price it, no questions filed."

bye.text: "Mind the grille." His eye is already back on the loupe, and on you.

dq_crack_accept.text: "Three," Hock says. "Open them where you like. Do not open them in here, I am not watching that."

dq_crack_done.text:
He goes over what you brought under the loupe, one at a time, unhurried, and pays each one at what it is. Nothing is worth a fortune. Everything is worth something.

"There," he says, and pushes the notes through the mesh. "Now you know. That is the entire service I provide and people find it disappointing every single time."

dq_crack_offer.text:
The loupe comes up. He does not answer for long enough that you check whether he heard.

"Sealed," he says at last. "A sealed thing is a rumour. I do not buy rumours. I buy objects, and an object has to have been LOOKED at before it is one."

He puts a small stack of notes on the mesh shelf and does not push it through.

"Three sleeves. Crack them. Bring me what is actually in your hand and I will pay you for that, and it will be a fair price, and you will know exactly what you sold."

He returns to the loupe.

"Sloat will pay you more. Sloat is paying for a feeling. I am not in that trade and I would not know how to price it."

dq_crack_sloat.text:
"He does." No heat in it at all. "He also has a back room with eleven hundred sealed sleeves in it that he cannot spend, cannot insure, and cannot open, because the moment he opens one it becomes worth what it is worth."

The loupe does not move.

"He is not a collector. He is a man holding his breath. It has been nine years."

He finally looks up.

"You can take his money. I will not think less of you and I will not do this deal afterwards. One or the other. That is not me being difficult, that is just what happens to the sleeves."

gossip.text: "I hear a great deal. I retain almost none of it. That's a service I provide." The loupe turns over in his fingers. "But some things stick to a man like lint."

options.label: "What do you make of the sealed card trade?"
options.text: "What do you make of the sealed card trade?"

options.label: You must hear things, back here.

root.text: Hock doesn't look up from the loupe. "Buying or selling? No, don't tell me, I can price a man from the door." He sets the loupe down. "I buy what you've stopped needing, I sell what someone else stopped needing, and I never once ask which of those it is. What's it to be."

whose.text: "Everyone's. No one's." He touches the watch in the case, almost gentle. "Every piece in here walked in on a bad week attached to a promise to come back for it. They mean it, every time. They don't come back, every time. I don't hold it against them. I just hold the goods." The loupe goes back in. "Now. Were you buying, or adding to the collection?"

clothing_layers: a shiny-elbowed pinstripe waistcoat over a collarless shirt
a jeweller's loupe on a greasy cord and fingerless gloves

name: Hock
